title: Screen Readers
definition: Software programs that allow blind or visually impaired users to read the text that is displayed on the computer screen with a speech synthesizer or braille display.
simpleExplanation: A screen reader is a robot that reads your website out loud. If you use a bunch of nested `<div>` tags with no text, the robot will just say 'group, group, group' and the user will have no idea what is happening. You must structure your React app logically.
realWorldExample: Using the `.sr-only` CSS class in Tailwind to visually hide a label like 'Search Bar', but keep it in the DOM so the screen reader announces it.

basic: What is `alt` text on an image?
intermediate: What happens if an image is purely decorative?
advanced: How do you announce dynamic React state changes to a screen reader?

answers.question: How do you announce dynamic changes?
answers.answer: Use an `aria-live` region. If a user submits a form and a success message appears, adding `aria-live='polite'` to the message container tells the screen reader to read the new text out loud without the user having to focus it.
